_note: Seeded by scripts/seed-retailers.ts, matched on slug. Whether a store is read is Malin's switch on /you/finder; "enabled" here only sets a newly added store's starting state. Wellington stores are shown as 'try on at' only once verified is true, and an address is only filled in after checking it on the retailer's own site, which `source` names. Checked 2026-11-04: Country Road's own store finder lists no NZ stores, so its store stays unverified; Checks Downtown (Auckland only) and Commoners (stockists only) have no Wellington store of their own; Barkers also has 82 Cuba Street and I Love Ugly 233 Lambton Quay, one store each is shown. Probed 2026-11-04: every Shopify feed below answers /products.json (or the listed men's collections), robots.txt allows it, and prices come back in the currency listed.

retailers.name: Patagonia
retailers.notes: The NZ site is its own Shopify shop priced in NZD; patagonia.com.au is a separate shop in AUD. The 'mens' collection is the men's range (about 1,070 products). Product types read like 'Medium,Bottoms & One Pieces', so the garment comes from the title; colours come from the variants' Color option and a colour: tag. Much of the range is technical kit the rules file as activewear. Probed 2026-11-05: robots.txt allows the feed, and a burst of requests is answered 429 with Retry-After 60, which the client waits out. Its store locator is drawn by script, so no Wellington store could be read from the site.

retailers.name: Bronze Snake
retailers.notes: A Melbourne label, one Shopify shop in AUD (its meta.json says so, and it lists NZ among the countries it ships to); there is no NZ site or market, so prices are AUD converted for display and shipping to NZ is extra. The 'mens' collection is the men's range (about 490 products); 'mens-new' is only its new arrivals. Probed 2026-11-07: robots.txt allows the feed, and a burst of requests is answered 429 with Retry-After 60, and after a whole-catalogue read it stayed limited for over an hour. Its stores are all in Australia.

retailers.name: LSKD
retailers.notes: Links only by default, Malin's call 2026-11-07: a Gold Coast activewear label, one Shopify shop in AUD (its meta.json says so, and it ships to NZ). A pasted link is read from /products/<handle>.js like any Shopify store, and a saved one is re-read each night. It starts switched off on /you/finder: its robots.txt disallows /collections/*/* (so no 'mens' collection feed), and the whole /products.json (about 4,900 products, 1,450 of them men's) tags every tee 'category:Tops > Tees & Tanks', which the rules read as tanks. Probed 2026-11-07: robots.txt allows /products/ and /products.json, and a burst of requests is answered 429 with Retry-After 60, and after a whole-catalogue read it stayed limited for over an hour. Its stores are in Australia and Auckland.

retailers.name: Rodd & Gunn
retailers.notes: Links only, for pieces he owns or wants: never walked and no switch on /you/finder, like Uniqlo. The site is Salesforce Commerce Cloud, not Shopify, so it has no products.json, and its catalogue is a page per colour (about 2,540 colours of 1,900 styles in the NZ sitemap, outlet included), which at one request a second would take most of an hour each night. A pasted link is read from its own page on the NZ site whatever region it was copied from (the ids are the same): a schema.org Product, the data layer's view_item, the usual price beside a sale price, the colour's photos and per-size stock. Trousers and jeans list each leg length as its own page and id; they are read together and stored as one colour. A link to a style with no colour chosen lists the colours to choose from. Every non-canonical product link answers 301 to the colour's own page; a colour no longer sold answers 410, and a saved one is then marked gone. A page priced in anything but NZD is refused. Probed 2026-11-05: robots.txt allows the product pages (it disallows the paginated category grids and the Product-Variation endpoint), and they answer the finder's own User-Agent with no challenge.

retailers.name: Uniqlo AU
retailers.notes: Links only, for pieces he owns or wants: Uniqlo has no NZ online store and does not ship here (its AU help centre says so), and the site is not Shopify, so the finder never walks it and it has no switch on /you/finder. A pasted link is read from its own region's store when it has one here (Uniqlo US), and from the Australian page for the same product otherwise, since it is the store added first on uniqlo.com. The page's HTML carries the product (colours, sizes, price, photos) in window.__PRELOADED_STATE__; per-size stock is not in it. Each colour is stored as its own product, as Country Road lists them. Probed 2026-11-05: robots.txt allows /au/en/products/, and the page answers the finder's own User-Agent.

retailers.name: Uniqlo US
retailers.notes: Links only, like Uniqlo AU, for a link copied from the US site: many US products and colours are not sold in Australia, and the Australian page for them is a 404 (checked 2026-11-05: three of six US shirts). Read from the US page in USD, shown in NZD. Does not ship to NZ. Probed 2026-11-05: robots.txt allows /us/en/products/, and the page answers the finder's own User-Agent with the same preloaded state as AU's.

retailers.name: Lululemon
retailers.notes: Added by hand only. The site is Salesforce Commerce Cloud, not Shopify, and Cloudflare answers every request but robots.txt with a challenge page (403), sitemap included, to the finder's own User-Agent; getting past it would mean posing as a browser, which the finder does not do. Its affiliate feed (Commission Factory) needs a public site to promote it from. So a Lululemon link pasted on Saved opens a form for the photo, name, kind, price, colour and size, and the price is never checked. Probed 2026-11-05. Its Wellington store could not be checked on its own site, so none is shown.
